key_insight: A topology-aware graph convolutional network can classify distribution-network faults accurately even when inverter-driven harmonic distortion and high photovoltaic penetration distort the signals.
engineering_relevance: This approach supports more reliable fault diagnosis in modern distribution grids with high renewable integration, improving protection performance under realistic operating stress.
method: Mapped pre-fault and post-fault voltage/current phasors, including harmonic components, onto the IEEE 34-bus network graph.
Trained a GCN on OpenDSS-generated scenarios spanning PV penetration levels of 30%, 50%, and 70% plus THD levels of 0%, 1%, 3%, and 5%.
Used differential evolution to tune the network, yielding a three-layer model optimized for fault classification.
evidence_signal: Across multiple fault classes and stressed conditions, the optimized GCN achieved an F1-score of 0.98 and outperformed CNN, LSTM, and MLP baselines, especially at 70% PV penetration with 5% THD.
watch_item: Performance depends on simulated OpenDSS data and IEEE 34-bus topology, so deployment on other feeders or with measurement noise may require retraining and validation.
paper_title: GCN-Based Model for Fault Classification in Distribution Networks under Harmonic Distortion
